title: Acquisition routes of cannabis and illegal substances in people with mental illness
summary:
The primary purpose of the study is to investigate the various pathways through which individuals with mental disorders in Germany acquire cannabis and other illegal substances. The study aims to gain a better understanding of these acquisition methods, the types of substances consumed, and the consumption patterns within this population. 

The background of the study is the high prevalence of cannabis and other illegal substance use among individuals with mental disorders. However, little is known about how these individuals obtain these substances and what role the presence of a mental disorder plays in their acquisitions. A better understanding of these aspects could contribute to the improvement of prevention and intervention measures. 

The study will use a specifically designed anonymous online questionnaire to collect data on the acquisition pathways of cannabis and illegal substances. The questionnaire will first be tested in Augsburg and then optimized if necessary. Following this, nationwide data collection will take place. participants will fill out the questionnaire only once. 

Potential participants of the study are adults in Germany who consume cannabis or other illegal substances. The study is aimed to both individuals with and without mental disorders to obtain a comprehensive picture if acquisition pathways and consumption patterns. 

The goals of the study are to identify the most common pathways for acquiring cannabis and illegal substances and to examine the association between these pathways and the presences of a mental disorder. The formulated hypotheses are as follows: "There is no difference in the acquisition pathways of illegal substances between individuals with lethal disorders and those without mental disorders (H0).", and "There is no difference in financial expenditures on illegal substances between individuals with mental disorders and those without mental disorders (H0)."
conditions: The study includes individuals with various mental disorders and substance dependencies, as well as individuals without any diagnosis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Individuals residing in Germany who consume or procure Cannabis or illegal substances.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals who do not reside in Germany and do not consume or procure Cannabis or illegal substances
